title: Purification of full-length recombinant human huntingtin proteins with allelic series of polyglutamine lengths
protocol: Add 100 ng of pFastBac1 plasmid containing the full-length HTT cDNA to 100 μL of DH10Bac™ competent cells.
Incubate the cells on ice for 30 min.
Heat-shock at 42°C for 45 s.
Incubate the cells on ice again for 2 min.
Add 900 μL of S.O.C. medium to the cells and incubate at 37°C for 4 h in a shaking incubator.
Prepare a series of 10×, 100×, and 1000× diluted cells with S.O.C. medium.
Plate 100 μL of each diluted cell sample on DH10Bac LB agar plates.
Incubate the plates for 2 days at 37°C in an incubator.
Pick 3–4 white colonies and restreak them onto new DH10Bac LB agar plates.
Incubate the restreaked plates for 2 days at 37°C.
Inoculate a single white colony into 5 mL of DH10Bac LB medium.
Incubate the culture for 2 days at 37°C in a shaking incubator.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 3,000×g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 300 μL of Sol I buffer.
Add 300 μL of Sol II buffer to the mixture and mix gently by inverting.
Incubate the sample at room temperature (RT; 20°C–24°C) for 5 minutes.
Add 300 μL of Sol III buffer to the mixture and mix gently by inverting.
Incubate the sample on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 17,000×g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer 750 μL of supernatant to 800 μL of 100% isopropanol and mix gently by inverting.
Incubate the sample on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the incubated sample at 17,000×g for 20 minutes at RT.
Decant the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of 70% ethanol on top of the white pellet.
Wash the pellet by inverting the tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 17,000×g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant with a pipette without disturbing the pellet.
Dry the white DNA pellet with air dry while the tubes are upside-down on a Kimwipe until the white pellet becomes transparent.
Dissolve the transparent DNA pellet by adding 40 μL of TE buffer.
Resuspend the DNA pellet gently by tapping.
Perform PCR using M13 forward and hHTT R146 primers.
Plate 1.0×10^6 Sf9 cells in 2 mL CCM3 media into each well in a 6-well plate.
Incubate the cells to attach to the bottom of the plate at 27°C for 1 h.
Prepare 1 μg of bacmid in 100 μL of CCM3 media and 6 μL of Cellfectin II in 100 μL of CCM3 media separately.
Combine the bacmid in CCM3 and the Cellfectin II in CCM3, mix gently by inverting.
Incubate the mixture for 45 min at RT.
Remove the medium from each well and add 2 mL of fresh CCM medium to each well.
Add 800 μL of fresh CCM medium to the mixture of bacmid and Cellfectin II, mix gently by inverting.
Remove the medium from each well again and add the bacmid-Cellfectin II mixture (∼1 mL) to the cells.
Incubate the plate at 27°C for 5 h.
Remove the medium after 5 h and add 2 mL of fresh CCM media to each well, incubate the plate at 27°C for 3 days.
Incubate the cell plate in a sealed chamber such as a Ziploc container with wet Kimwipes during incubation.
Collect the medium containing baculovirus from the wells after 3 days of incubation.
Filter the collected medium using a 0.22 μm syringe filter to obtain P1 virus stock.
Plate 5×10^6 Sf9 cells in 10 ml into a 75 cm² cell culture T-flask or 10 cm² dish.
Wait for 30 min to allow the cells to attach to the bottom of the plate.
Add 50 μl of harvested P1 virus to the cells and gently shake the flask to mix the virus with the media.
Incubate the flask at 27°C for 3–5 days.
Check the condition of infected cells compared with control to confirm baculovirus infection.
Collect baculovirus-infected Sf9 cells after 5 days post-infection with P2 virus.
Filter the collected media using Steriflip filter unit (Merck Millipore).
Plate 15×10^6 Sf9 cells in 25 mL into a 150 cm² cell culture dish, achieving a final concentration of 0.6×10^6 cells/mL.
Incubate the plated cells at 27°C for 5-6 days to allow infection and observe cellular changes.
Centrifuge the media at 4,000×g for 10 min after observing cell detachment and floating.
Filter the supernatant using a 0.22 μm bottle top filter (PES, Corning) to obtain the P3 virus stock.
Store the prepared virus stocks at 4°C and protect from light.
Note: The stored virus can be used within one month for protein expression without significant loss of efficacy.
Prepare cells in 1,000 mL of CCM3 media in a 2,800 mL Fernbach flask for large-scale infection.
Incubate the cells until reaching a density of 2.0–2.5×10^6 cells/mL at 27°C with 100 rpm in an orbital shaker incubator.
Add 50 mL of P3 virus to 1,000 mL of cells in a 2,800 mL Fernbach flask once the proper cell density is reached.
Incubate for 42–48 hours at 27°C.
Centrifuge the cells at 4,600×g for 20 minutes at 4°C to harvest them.
Decant the medium and resuspend the cell pellet with 30 mL of the cell harvest buffer containing 1 mM PMSF and final 1× Protease inhibitor Cocktail.
Wash the surface of the cell pellet with the cell harvest buffer before resuspending the cells.
Freeze the resuspended cells in liquid nitrogen and store them at -80°C.
Reconstitute cells by repeatedly freezing and thawing in liquid nitrogen and in a water bath at 25°C for three cycles.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 27,000×g for 2 hours using 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
If necessary, centrifuge again under the same conditions for an additional hour to ensure clarity of supernatant.
Collect clear supernatant without disturbing the soft pellet.
Equilibrate anti-FLAG M2 affinity resin with wash buffer A.
Distribute 10 mL of equilibrated M2 resin equally among the supernatants.
Incubate the mixture of supernatant and M2 resin for 3 hours at 4°C on a tube rotator or tumbler rotating at 10 turns per minute.
Collect the M2 resin by centrifugation at 1,500×g for 5 minutes.
Slowly pour out the supernatant from the centrifuged M2 resin.
Collect all the M2 resin in a single 50 mL tube with wash buffer A and bring the solution to 50 mL by adding wash buffer A.
Centrifuge the collected M2 resin at 1,500×g for 5 minutes.
Decant the supernatant from the centrifuged M2 resin.
Add 40 mL of wash buffer A to the M2 resin and resuspend by inverting the tube.
Repeat steps for washing with wash buffer A three times.
Repeat steps for washing with wash buffer B three times.
Repeat steps for washing with wash buffer C three times.
Repeat steps for washing with wash buffer B three times.
Repeat steps for washing with wash buffer A three times.
Load the M2 resin to an Econo-Column® Chromatography Column, 2.5 × 10 cm.
Wash the resin with wash buffer A until the absorbance of the flow-through is lower than 0.01 at OD280 reading.
Decant the wash buffer A to the surface of the M2 resin.
Add 1 column volume (CV, 10 mL) of the M2 elution buffer slowly on top of the resin without disturbing it and incubate for 10 minutes.
Collect the incubated elution buffer.
Repeat steps for collecting eluted samples until the OD280 reading is less than 0.01.
Remove the N-terminal tags of HTT with TEV protease.
Collect the eluted samples and add TEV protease.
Add 40 μg of TEV protease per 1 mg of the eluted samples (800 μg of TEV protease for 20 mg of HTT protein).
Transfer the sample with TEV protease to Spectra/Por® 1 Dialysis membrane (30 Kd MWCO).
Dialyze the sample for 12–16 h against 2 L of dialysis buffer.
Load Ni-nitrilotriacetic acid resin (Ni-NTA, Qiagen) to an Econo column (2.5×10 cm).
Ensure Ni-NTA is resistant to 1 mM DTT and 0.5 mM EDTA in the dialysis buffer.
Equilibrate the Ni-NTA resin with the dialysis buffer.
Load the sample through the equilibrated Ni-NTA column and collect the flow-through.
Reload the collected flow-through to the Ni-NTA again.
Repeat loading and collecting the flow-through for 3 times.
Concentrate the sample using an Amicon Ultra 100-KDa filter up to 10 mL by repeated centrifugation at 1,500×g for 5 min each time.
Pipette the samples after every centrifuge cycle.
Equilibrate a Superdex 200 HiLoad 26/60 column with gel filtration buffer.
Load the concentrated sample from step #77 onto the equilibrated column.
Run the column at a flow rate of 2.0 mL/min and collect fractions in 5 mL increments.
Evaluate the purity of each fraction by SDS-PAGE.
Collect the fractions containing HTT proteins.
Concentrate the collected fractions using an Amicon Ultra 100-KDa filter up to 5 mg/mL concentration.
Aliquot the concentrated sample into approximately 20 μL per tube.
Snap freeze the aliquots with liquid nitrogen.
Store the samples at -80°C.
Centrifuge thawed proteins at 17,000×g for 20 minutes at 4°C to remove any precipitate.
